chapter_theme: A song at Veppur (வேப்பூர்): the poet asks Murugan to speak to him with his own word the form of the experience that shines to those who, with both kinds of deeds gone, sleep in awareness; the praise names the burning of the sea and the demons' widows entering the fire.

753.reading: The poet asks that, rather than tending the hut that carries life and dances in this sea-girt world and the dark-eyed people with their quarrels, he be told by Murugan's own holy word the form of the experience (அநுபூதி) that shines only to those who, both kinds of deeds ended, sleep in awareness. The praise names an episode of the Kuru clan, the wives of the night-roaming demons leaping into fire while Indra's city prospers, the vel that set the sea ablaze to its depths, and Veppur, whose fertile fields end want in the seven worlds.
753.nuance: இருவினையற உணர்வொடு தூங்குவார்க்கே விளங்கும் அநுபூதி: the state is open only to those in whom good and bad deeds have ceased and who sleep yet are aware, a known description of the knower's waking sleep. The plea is for teaching by word (வாக்கால் மொழிந்தருள). குருகுல வேந்து தேர்ப்பாகன் மைந்தன் probably alludes to Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer, but how the phrase splits and whose son is meant is unclear.

links.note: 753 says the experience (அநுபூதி) shines only to those who, both kinds of deeds ended, sleep with awareness (இருவினையற உணர்வொடு தூங்குவார்க்கே விளங்கும்). Tirumanthiram 129 says that in sleep they saw Sivaloka, Siva-yoga and Siva-bhoga within themselves, and asks how that state could be told (தூங்கிக் கண்டார் ... நிலை சொல்வது எவ்வாறே). Both name the waking sleep of the knower as where the experience is found; the song adds the condition that deeds have ceased and asks to be told by Murugan's word what the verse says cannot be told.
